preamble: Alphabetical jigsawMethod: solve the clues and fit the solutions into the diagram wherever they will go.

clue.text: Put a gloss on Europeans

parts.note: the French are one European people
the Polish are another European people

explanation.surface: Someone is putting a favourable spin on the people of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, Europeans, supplies two nationalities side by side; capitalise neither and they make a woodworking verb.
explanation.definitionFit: French polishing is building up a high shine on wooden furniture with shellac, which puts a glossy finish on it.

clue.text: Doting pangolin's food melts in the mouth

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the sweet rather than a noun

parts.note: doting on someone is being very fond of them
pangolins live on ants and termites

explanation.surface: A devoted pangolin offers up its dinner, which dissolves deliciously on the tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Fondant is a soft sugar paste confection, its French name meaning melting, which dissolves readily on the tongue.

clue.text: Obliterate the former word play on Earth

parts.note: ex- is the prefix for what used to be
a pun is play on words
Ge, or Gaia, is the Greek earth goddess, and ge- the prefix for earth

explanation.surface: Wipe out an old word game that was played on this planet.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, on means placed above, so the pun sits over GE.
explanation.definitionFit: To expunge is to erase or strike out completely, which is wiping something out of existence.

clue.text: Effect of wagon wheels on paper

parts.note: a cart is a farm wagon
the effect of heavy traffic on a soft track is raised ridges between the ruts

explanation.surface: What happens when wagon wheels run over a sheet of paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The wheels belong to the cart: a cart ridge is the mound its wheels leave, and the two words run together.
explanation.definitionFit: Cartridge paper is a thick, rough-textured drawing paper, originally used for making gun cartridges.

clue.text: Tommy's correspondent turns up without fuel

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other
turns tells us the following short word flips round to read the other way

parts.note: taken as written
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A British soldier's pen pal arrives with nothing to burn.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tommy is a British private soldier; his French counterpart in the First World War was the POILU, literally 'hairy one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Poilu was the nickname of the French infantryman, the corresponding figure to the British Tommy Atkins.

clue.text: Compared German song with interior knowledge

indicators.note: having something as its interior means the song is wrapped round the other piece

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song
ken is knowledge, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: Someone compared a German song, praising its insight into the inner self.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to compare them, pointing out a similarity between them.

clue.text: Go round, going round again to get vegetable from water

indicators.note: going round means one piece encircles the other

parts.note: to skirt something is to go round its edge
re- is the prefix for again

explanation.surface: A circling instruction leads, after another lap, to a vegetable fished out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: Go round and going round sit side by side, but only the second is the instruction; the first is a verb to be translated.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirret is an old root crop of the water-parsnip genus Sium, a plant that grows naturally in wet ground.

clue.text: Chess player's choice portion, in which I telephone round the world

indicators.note: the portion is the container that the following pieces sit in

parts.note: a whack is a share or portion, as in 'a fair whack'
taken as written

indicators.note: the abbreviation for telephone goes round, enclosing, the word for the world

parts.note: the orb is the globe, the world

explanation.surface: A chess player, deciding which side to take, phones around the world to ask advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chess player's choice' is the colour of the pieces; the nested containers build the middle before the portion wraps it.
explanation.definitionFit: Before a chess game a player chooses, or is assigned, which colour of pieces to play with.

clue.text: Paper basket for a scruff needing time outside

indicators.note: outside means the time abbreviation is split to wrap the other piece

parts.note: HR is the abbreviation for hour
the scruff of the neck is the nape

explanation.surface: A wastepaper basket is wanted for some untidy person who needs a time-out.
explanation.walkthrough: Scruff looks like an untidy person, but it is the back of the neck.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanaper was a wicker case for keeping documents, which gave its name to an old Chancery office.

clue.text: A hint joining head to heart

indicators.note: the first letter of the word, its head, travels into its middle, its heart

parts.note: joining means linking

explanation.surface: A tip on how to connect the head with the heart, intellect with emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The L at the head of LINKING moves to the centre of the word, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An inkling is a slight suggestion or faint notion, much like a hint of something.

clue.text: Textbook written by poet for 60% of hospital — good gracious!

parts.note: Thomas Gray, the 18th-century English poet of the Elegy Written in a Country Churchyard

indicators.note: sixty per cent of a ten-letter word is its first six letters

parts.note: a sanatorium is a hospital for convalescents or the chronically ill
'My!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'good gracious!'

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a textbook by a poet that covers most of what a hospital does.
explanation.walkthrough: '60% of' keeps SANATO, the first six of SANATORIUM's ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray's Anatomy is the classic anatomy textbook used by medical students since 1858.

clue.text: Person responsible for stable footwear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who prepares racehorses

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of firm, sturdy shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A racehorse trainer runs a yard of horses, and trainers is the British name for sports shoes or sneakers.

clue.text: Bones somewhat vulnerable to song?

indicators.note: somewhat means only some of the following word is kept, the rest discarded

parts.note: taken as written; only letters two to four survive
an aria is a song in an opera

explanation.surface: Are bones liable to be damaged by singing?
explanation.definitionFit: Ulnaria is the plural of ulnare, a wrist bone on the little-finger side next to the forearm's ulna.

clue.text: Strange variation of route

indicators.note: a variation is a changed version, so the letters come in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An odd alternative way of getting somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Outré, borrowed from French, describes something unconventional or eccentric, beyond the bounds of the usual.

clue.text: Reporter of cereal-eating ungulate is stupid and is fond

parts.note: dozy is British slang for slow-witted
someone who dotes is very fond

explanation.surface: A grazing animal's spokesman is called foolish and sentimental.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1940s novelty song Mairzy Doats runs 'mares eat oats and does eat oats', sung as 'mairzy doats and dozy doats'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the song, the lyric slurs 'does eat oats', so it tells us of female deer eating oats.

clue.text: This sort of puzzle starts after alien enters regions of a star

indicators.note: the alien and the starting letters go into the regions, as a visitor enters a place

parts.note: zones are regions

indicators.note: the starting letters come after the alien

parts.note: ET, the extra-terrestrial of the film, is an alien
this puzzle is an Alphabetical Jigsaw, as its preamble says, and those words start with these letters

explanation.surface: A puzzle begins once an extraterrestrial invades parts of a star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This sort of puzzle' points to the preamble: this is an Alphabetical Jigsaw, whose initials are what 'starts' takes.
explanation.definitionFit: Catherine Zeta-Jones is a Welsh film actress, an Oscar-winning star of Chicago.

clue.text: Search for somewhere for a cow, if you're asked

parts.note: a byre is a cowshed
a quest is a search

explanation.surface: Looking for a place to keep a cow, should anyone want one.
explanation.walkthrough: Search for X puts the search after X, so BYRE comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by request means doing it because someone has asked for it to be done.

clue.text: For ever sighing for a part in the game

indicators.note: a part in says the letters sit within the words before it

parts.note: letters running across the three words

explanation.surface: Eternally longing to be given a role in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Reversi is a board game, also sold as Othello, in which captured discs are flipped to the opposite colour.

clue.text: Designer edition propelled by manpower

parts.note: Mary Quant was the fashion designer behind the miniskirt
ED is the abbreviation for edition

explanation.surface: A fashion designer's version was powered by human muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: A quant is a punting pole used on East Anglian barges.
explanation.definitionFit: To quant a boat is to push it along with a long pole, so it moves by human effort alone.

clue.text: Hermia at school achieved 5-9 points

parts.note: V is five in Roman numerals
IX is nine in Roman numerals
E and N are compass points

explanation.surface: A schoolgirl scored five to nine marks.
explanation.walkthrough: In A Midsummer Night's Dream Helena says of Hermia, 'She was a vixen when she went to school'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Helena describes the young Hermia as a vixen, a quarrelsome, spiteful girl.

clue.text: Small cavity found by a copper in a rodent

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the animal

parts.note: a vole is a small rodent
taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer discovers a little hole inside a rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests a policeman; here it is the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuole is a tiny space within a cell, enclosed by membrane and filled with fluid.

clue.text: Endangered predator takes up wind instrument, keeping one piano on call

indicators.note: the turned instrument holds the following pieces inside it
in a down clue, taking up lifts the word so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: sax is short for saxophone, a wind instrument
the Roman numeral for one is I
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
'hi' is a call of greeting

explanation.surface: A threatened hunter picks up a saxophone, holding a piano note to call out.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'takes up' means reading upwards, so the instrument is reversed before it holds the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Xiphias is the genus of the swordfish, a large predatory fish whose stocks have been overfished.

clue.text: You 'ave to bisect a line to find a beehive

indicators.note: the dropped aitch in 'ave tells us to drop the H in the same way

parts.note: to bisect is to cut in two
taken as written
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Cockney advice: cut a line in half and you will find a hive of bees.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken with a dropped aitch, halve becomes 'alve.
explanation.definitionFit: Alveary is an old word for a beehive, from the Latin alvearium, a place where bees are kept.

clue.text: Writer of the "Carry On" genre

indicators.note: of the says the letters are drawn from within the quoted words that follow

parts.note: letters spanning the end of one word to the start of another

explanation.surface: Who wrote those British comedy films in the Carry On series?
explanation.walkthrough: Carry On films were a long-running series of bawdy British comedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte M. Yonge was a prolific Victorian novelist, best known for The Heir of Redclyffe.

clue.text: Objects of bowls and billiards fortunately hit

parts.note: the jack is the small ball bowlers aim at
to pot is to sink a ball in billiards

explanation.surface: Bowls and billiards both have targets that a lucky player may strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the jackpot means winning a big prize by luck, so the word stands for a lucky strike.

clue.text: What makes a tinker horny?

indicators.note: makes in the sense of forms or produces, so the letters are made into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about what arouses a travelling pot-mender.
explanation.walkthrough: Horny means made of horn; a tinker is a travelling mender of pots and pans.
explanation.definitionFit: Keratin is the protein forming horn, hair and nails, so it is what turns any tissue horny.

clue.text: There's magic for all in the match game — metal formed by tears?

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the game

parts.note: Nim is a game played by taking matches from piles
obi, or obeah, is West Indian folk magic
U is the film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A conjuring trick open to everyone in a game of matches, and a metal born of weeping.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all audiences.
explanation.definitionFit: Niobium was named after Niobe, the mythical mother who wept endlessly for her slain children.

clue.text: Don't be so concerned with the head's stupidity

parts.note: to mind less is to be less bothered
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: Advice to stop worrying about the headteacher's foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mindlessness is thoughtless lack of intelligence, so the word serves as a synonym for foolishness.
